items.title: CVE-2026-113877: HTTP::Headers::ActionPack versions before 0.10 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via Accept-Language ranges matched as regular expressions
items.one_liner: Review Perl applications using HTTP::Headers::ActionPack for unescaped Accept-Language parsing to prevent DoS.
items.summary: HTTP::Headers::ActionPack versions before 0.10 for Perl contain a CPU exhaustion vulnerability caused by unescaped Accept-Language header ranges being interpolated directly into regular expressions. Because the input is not sanitized, a remote attacker can supply a malicious range like `(a?|b?){26}z` to trigger exponential backtracking or make the parsing function die. Applications that pass untrusted Accept-Language headers to this library are vulnerable to denial of service. The issue is resolved by upgrading to version 0.10 or later.
key_facts: CWE: CWE-624 Executable Regular Expression Error
items.bottom_line: Unsanitized Accept-Language ranges in HTTP::Headers::ActionPack < 0.10 allow remote CPU exhaustion via regex backtracking.

items.title: CVE-2026-114053 (CRITICAL 9.2): vLLM from 0.7.3 before 0.31.0 forwards the request-supplied mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision to Transformers…
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-114053 enables unauthenticated RCE via malicious model code revisions in vulnerable vLLM deployments.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability identified as CVE-2026-114053 with a CVSS score of 9.2 exists in vLLM versions 0.7.3 up to 0.31.0. The flaw allows request-supplied `mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision` values to be forwarded to Transformers `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained`, permitting clients to choose which revision of a model's dynamic processor code is imported when `trust_remote_code` is enabled. An attacker controlling a revision in a served model repository can exploit this by sending a malicious multimodal request to the unauthenticated `/tokenize` endpoint to achieve arbitrary Python code execution inside the vLLM API process.
items.bottom_line: vLLM instances between versions 0.7.3 and 0.31.0 allow unauthenticated remote code execution via the /tokenize endpoint if remote code execution is trusted.

items.one_liner: A critical CVSS 10.0 regular expression integer overflow in GitLab allows unauthenticated RCE across 12 years of self-managed releases.
items.summary: GitLab has patched a maximum-severity CVSS 10.0 vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-110264, which allows unauthenticated remote code execution on self-managed instances across every version released over the past 12 years going back to version 7.0. The flaw is caused by an integer overflow during the compilation of crafted regular expressions within Ruby's built-in Onigmo engine, which GitLab bundles in its packages. While GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already patched, self-managed administrators must upgrade immediately, as earlier patches from October 12 did not cover versions prior to 19.2. GitLab has backported fixes to branches 18.11, 19.0, 19.1, and 19.2, and released Sigma detection rules to help identify exploitation attempts.

items.title: Cisco Secure Client Secure Firewall Posture Module Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A local privilege escalation bug in Cisco Secure Client's posture module lets attackers achieve root or SYSTEM privileges.
items.summary: A high-severity privilege escalation vulnerability exists in the interprocess communication channel of the Secure Firewall Posture module in Cisco Secure Client due to insufficient validation of user-supplied input. An authenticated local attacker can exploit this flaw by sending crafted IPC messages to a local socket, allowing them to execute limited file writes with SYSTEM or root privileges. On macOS and Linux, this vulnerability can be leveraged to achieve full root privileges, prompting Cisco to assign it a High Security Impact Rating. Software updates have been released by Cisco to address the issue, as no workarounds are available.
key_facts: Affected Product: Cisco Secure Client (Secure Firewall Posture module)
Impact: SYSTEM or root privilege escalation
items.bottom_line: Cisco Secure Client users must update immediately to patch an IPC input validation flaw that allows local attackers to escalate to root or SYSTEM privileges.

items.title: MemTensor/MemT-1.0 — Official repository for MemT-1.0
items.summary: MemT-1.0 is a new generation of memory foundation models that makes persistent, dynamically evolving memory an intrinsic part of model computation. MemT-1.0 integrates dynamic local memory and trainable hyper memory to retain and leverage historical information without accessing original context at inference. Its persistent state remains constant in size, reducing storage by approximately 66× versus full-context KV cache at 128K history length. The project makes three main contributions: - Memory architecture. Introduce MemT-1.0 with improved memory storage and utilization, and Mixture-of-Storage (MoS) for scalable memory capacity.
